chunks: A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad al-Barqī, from Jaʿfar ibn al-Muthannā al-Khaṭīb, who said:

I was in al-Madīnah, and the roof of the mosque that overlooked the grave had fallen, and the workers were going up and down while we were a group. So I said to our companions, “Which of you has an appointment to enter upon Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام tonight?” Mihrān ibn Abī Naṣr said, “I do,” and Ismāʿīl ibn ʿAmmār al-Ṣayrafī said, “I do.” So we said to them both, “Ask him for us about climbing up so that we may look over the grave of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله.”

Then when the next day came, we met the two of them and all gathered together. Ismāʿīl said, “We asked him for you about what you mentioned, and he said: ‘I do not like for any of them to rise above him, and I do not regard him as safe from seeing something by which his eyesight may depart, or seeing him standing and performing salat (prayer), or seeing him with one of his wives, صلى الله عليه وآله.’”

key_terms.أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: a title of Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام
key_terms.الصُّعُودِ: climbing upward to a higher place
key_terms.الْقَبْرِ: the grave of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله
key_terms.الْمَسْجِدِ: the mosque in al-Madīnah connected with the Prophet’s grave
key_terms.يَعْلُوَ: to rise above or be elevated over

ai.seo_question: Why did Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام forbid climbing above the grave of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله?
ai.summary: This hadith relates a report from Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام discouraging people from climbing above the grave of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله. It indicates reverence for the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله after his earthly life and warns that such an act may expose a person to overwhelming unseen realities.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Al Barqy, from Ja’far Bin Al Musna Al Khateeb who said,

‘I was in Al-Medina and the ceiling of the Masjid which was upon the grave had fallen, and the workers were ascending and descending, and we were a group. So I said to our companions, ‘Whom from you all to seek an appointment for him to see Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> tonight?’ So Mihran Bin Abu Nasr said, ‘I do’. And Ismail Bin Ammar Al-Sayrafi said, ‘I do’. So we said to them both, ‘You both ask him<sup>asws</sup> for us about the ascending to see above the grave of the Prophet<sup>saww</sup>’.

So when it was the morning, we met up with them both, and all of us had gathered. So Ismail said, ‘We had asked himasws for you all about what you had mentioned, so heasws said: ‘Iasws do not like it for anyone from you that he should be higher above himsaww, and there is no safety for him that he should see something due to which his eyesight would go away, or he may see himsaww standing praying Salat, or he might see himsaww along with one of hissaww wives’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Barqi from Ja‘far ibn al-Muthanna al-Khatib who has said the following.

“I was in Madina when the roof over the grave of the Holy Prophet (s.a) had crumbled down and the workers were climbing up and down (for repairs). We were a group and said to our people, “Who has an appointment with abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.)?” Mihran ibn abu Nasr said, “I have an appointment with the Imam (a.s.).” ’Isma‘il ibn ‘Ammar al-Sayrafi said, “I have an appointment with the Imam (a.s.).” I said to them, “Ask the Imam (a.s.) if it is permissible to climb up and look on to the grave of the Holy Prophet (s.a).”

Next day we met them and we all came together. ’Isma‘il said, “We asked your question and he said this. “I do not like anyone to climb over him and I do not feel safe for anyone whose eye sight may go away because of catching sight of something that cause him such loss or see him standing in prayer or see him with anyone of his wives.”
